full_judgment:
The entire 23.13 acre 'Ka' schedule suit land of Title Suit No. 23 of 2008 appertaining to C.S. khatian No. 07 of Mouza Chandona being projabili property under the previous Bhawal Jaminder. Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury and others represented by court of words. the then government for the purpose of acquisition of rent receiving interest of the said jaminder, at first, published projabili property gazette notification under section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, shortly SAT-Act, 1950 on 24.03.1952 (Exhibit 7), describing therein the schedules of projabili properties and thereafter, the government after paying compensation to the said jaminder for acquisition of rent receiving interest of their projabili property cited in the said projabili gazette, published compensation payment gazetee on 29.02.1956 (Exhibit-9) declaring compensation had been paid to the jaminders as per compensation, when the Government prepared and published S.A. khatian No. 63 (Exhibit-1) connecting with the suit property was duly prepared and published in the names of the previous joint projas, Chan Miah and Basaruddin in equal /8/ (eight) annas share; after scrutinizing the concerned projabili property papers and documents connected with the suit property remained in the sherestha/ custody of the jaminder and thereafter, the Revenue Department of the Government, like title register of the then jaminder, Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury represented by Court of Wards (Exhibit-4), projabili property gazette (Exhibit-9) etc. upgrading their status from projas to owners. The government not only prepared and published S.A. khatian No. 63 (Exhibit-1) in the names of the previous projas, Chan Miah and Basaruddin as equal /8/ (eight) annas owners upgrading their status as owners but also inserted their names in the Register-II, Talab Baki Register (Exhibit-5), as rent payees in equal shares to the Government Revenue Department. Further case of them is that, on amicable partition Basaruddin got in total 5.40 acre 'Kha' schedule 6 piece properties in his /8/ (eight) annas share. wherein he and thereafter on his demised, the present plaintiffs appellants petitioners as his heirs have been owning, and possessing by erecting and constructing homestead in the 'Kha (2 )' schedule suit property and by opening holding No. 220, Laxmipura, under Gazipur Municipality against it and by paying taxes and deferent bills like electricity, Titas Gas etc. taken against the said holding No. 220 (exhibit-13 series) and the rest 'Kha( I)', 'Kha(3)', 'Kha(4)', 'Kha (5)', and 'Kha (6)', schedules as agricultural lands and ponds by way of cultivating and by rearing fish; inspite of acquisition of ownership and possession as stated herein above by operation of SAT Act. 1950 in the 'Kha' schedule 6 piece properties, the opposite party No. 1, Mr. Abdur Rouf claining himself as manager of Court of Wards, the defendant. No. 14 of Title Suit No. 23 of 2008 and also claiming as shebayet of Sree Sree Madhab Bigraha, defendant No. 1 of said title suit No. 23 of 2008, opposite party No.2 and 3 of the present petition, came to `Kha' schedule suit properties on 12.12.2007 and expressed to the petitioners that family deity Madhab Bigraha, the defendant No.. 1 through his representation as shebayet, got a decree of declaration of title and recovery of khan possession of total 18.73 acres land out of 'Ka' scheduled 23.13 acres land including the petitioner's 'Kha' scheduled 6 piece 5.40 acres properties in Title Suit No. 1219 of 1985 of the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Gazipur against some third parties, Chan Miah and others and asked the petitioners to handover possession of the said 'Kha' scheduled 6 pieces properties in favour of decree holder, Sree Sree Madhab Bigraha, through him as shebayet; that the petitioners after knowing about the aforesaid decree passed in Title Suit No. 1219 of 1985, filed Title Suit No. 23 of 2008 challenging the said decree as fraudulent, collusive and not binding upon them along with other consequential reliefs of confirmation of possession and permanent injunction on 06.01.2008. 

 5. In the said suit the petitioners as plaintiffs filed an application under Order XXXIX Rule 1 and 2 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for ad-interim and temporary injunction on the next day on 07.01.2008 praying for restraining defendant No. 1, Madhab Bigraha and defendant No. 14, Court of Words, Bhawal Raj Estate stating the self same facts of acquisition of title and possession by operation SAT Act. 1950, as stated in the plaint. 

 33. We have scrutinized the said section and found that the section is applicable in case of the property remained in charge of the court of wards and if the said property is transferred by the court of wards to some third party by sale, gift or by any other modes of transfer, then for giving delivery of possession of such transferred property to said transferee, the court of wards can exercise such power of eviction as stated. Section 18(A) was inserted in the Court of Wards Act after SAT Act. 1950, stating that, the court of wards can keep in its charge only the retainable khas land after acquisitioning rent receiving interest of the rent receiver over its projabili property by the Government under SAT Act, 1950. The petitioners property appertaining to C.S Khatian No. 7 having found at page 492 of projabill property Gazette, it can never be in-charge of the Court of Wards and claiming title therein by the Court of Wards would be another contempt of court as per judgment of the High Court Division as well as Appellate Division of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of Bangladesh. It may be further stated that in its written statements, had never claimed suit property appertaining to C.S. khatian No.7 as of its own property, rather claimed as property of private deity of Sree Sree Madhab Bigraha and said Bigraha got decree in Title Suit No. 1219 of 1985, through its so called shebayet Abdur Rod, the Manager, Court of Wards, on 24.10.1996 

 34. On the other hand, the Assistant Manager, Court of Wards, Bhawal Raj Estate, Mr.Sabbir Ahmed as D.W- I , in his cross examination at one time stated that the deity is a family deity of the Wards of Court of. Wards and the said deity has no taken any tenancy settlement of the suit land from the Court of Wards and is also not the owner and possessor of the Suit property; rather, the Court of Wards is the owner of the suit property and in another time, he stated that deity is the owner of the suit property. From his said contradictory statements it can easily be concluded that neither the deity nor the Court of Wards was ever owner in possession of the suit property. Since the suit property is cited in the projabili property Gazette, at pa 492 (Ext-5) and from the exhibit-4 title registrar of the jaminder and Ext-5, the register II of the Revenue Department of the Government and other documents like S.A Khatian, C.A Roll etc the name of the petitioners' predecessor Basiruddin is found to have been cited, as proja under the jamindar Bhawal Court of Wards, it can never be owned either by the Wards through Court of Wards, Bhawal Raj Estate as it is barred by section 3(2) of the SAT Act, 1950 and 8(A) of the Court of Wards Act 1879 and also by P.O 90 of 1972 or by the deity as its own property. Moreover, the system of management and administration of the property of the deity and that of the Court of Wards are distinct and different to each other, as the first. one is managed and administered as per Endowment Act, 1863 and second one is managed and administered by Court of Wards Act, 1879 as of private person's property. So, in no circumstances the Government Property Recovery Act, 1970 can be applicable in case of the kha(2)' schedule suit property. So, starting of eviction case No.03/06 under the Government property recovery Act, 1970 and evicted the petitioners from their 'kha(2)' schedule private property by using Government machineries is beyond the jurisdiction of Court of Wards and also of the Deputy Commissioner of Gazipur. 

 35. The Learned Advocate of the petitioners, Mr. Md. Khalilur Rahman submitted that during the pendency of this rule the Court of Wards Bhawal Raj Estate had changed their views in claiming their title over its projabili property as cited in the Projabili property Gazette published on 24.03.1952 by the Government under section 3(A) of the SAT Act 1950. following the decisions, observations  and directions of the Hon'ble Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh reported in 31 DLR (S/C) page -13, 53 and 14 MLR (A/D) page - 40 and also the judgment passed in writ petition No. 17056 and 17216 of 2012 by the High Court Division. He further submitted that the Court of Wards had already given under takings in Contempt Petition No.226 of 2013 and 346 of 2013 to the effect that they would not make any further claim over its projabili property cited in the projabili property Gazette in future and also begged apology for making such claim over the projabili property. Their Lordships Mr. Justice Mr. Miza Hossain Haider and Mr. Khurshed Adam Sarker in their judgment dated 10.02.2014 though accepted their apology but had given warning to the Court of Wards not to claim over its projabili properties cited in the projabili property Gazette in future. The petitioner's property appertaining to C.S khatian No.7 of Mouza Chandona, being cited at page 492 of said projabili property Gazette (Exhibit-7) the petitioners filed an application on 18.02.2014 before us for knowing the view of the present Chairman, Land Reform Board in respect of Court of Wards' projabili properties, upon whom the Management and administration of the court of Wards has been bestowed by the Government. But on the vehement protest raised by Mr. Nurul Amin, Advocate, his view could not be ascertained. So, we have been compelled to take up the violation rule for hearing and heard for days together.
